questions: How many bars, chips and cooldowns did you measure, and how many showed the zero-field diode and its reversal with preparation field? The paper shows two bars (Fig. 3 and Extended Data Fig. 4).
Why were any others set aside?

Which ranges did you measure beyond the ones shown: preparation fields above ±1 T along [100], η against small applied fields near zero, and temperatures between 20 mK and Tc? Does η change with the 50 µV threshold or the 0.2 s step delay?
What does the second-best dataset look like, for example a repeat of the Fig. 3d loop, or the switching-current distributions and Fig. 3b-type data for the [100] bar?
Did the bar stay below Tc between each preparation excursion and the readout at H = 0, and what happens to η if you warm above Tc and cool back at zero field before reading it?
What is the field at the sample at nominal H = 0 after the ±1 T and ±4 T excursions, and how did you calibrate it? Was the magnet in a known state before the zero-field cooldown of Fig. 3a?

Were the [010] and [100] bars on the same chip, so that the [100] axis lay along the same magnet coil in both? A cooldown with the chip turned by 90° would separate the crystal axis from the magnet axis.

At what temperature and field history was the SQUID bound of Fig. 2b taken, and does the 2 nm heterostructure itself show the Fig. 4 hysteresis? The reference bar came from "a CuMnAs wafer with 3 nm fully oxidized Al cap" (p. 8).
